scope: Local automated behavior and actual Chromium encoder dimension control; not a physical FPS or network acceptance claim
changes: Selected capture dimensions/FPS on initial publication, then capture constraints and proportional encoder caps before successful start returns.
Five-second diagnostic polling; three consecutive drift observations trigger at most one automatic repair per current profile and track generation.
Lower adaptive output, inactive layers and absent output measurements do not trigger forced quality increases.
User changes serialize after in-flight writes; stop/replacement/profile generations invalidate stale observations and pending mutations.
Persistent warning after failed recovery; validated guard outcomes and capture settings included in media.sample.

chromium_encoding_smoke.source: Synthetic 2560x1440 canvas at 5fps; two local RTCPeerConnections; no application account or production SFU
chromium_encoding_smoke.isolation: Test-only maintain-resolution isolates dimension controls from congestion adaptation. Production maintains its existing maintain-framerate policy.
chromium_encoding_smoke.first_attempt: With default balanced adaptation, Chromium encoded 480x270 despite correct 1920x1080 capture and sender caps; this correctly demonstrates why lower adaptive output must not cause repair.

checks.local_full_contract_wrapper: BLOCKED on Windows by existing tools.audio.test_asset_build hardcoded /source path assertion; the direct OpenAPI check passed. Full Linux contracts remain a release gate.

limitations: This receipt predates trusted CI and deployment; delivery must be bound to the final source revision separately.
getSettings().frameRate describes capture settings, not measured captured-frame throughput.
Existing browser tabs require reload and a new share to exercise the new initial-publication code.
Physical moving-content FPS, Safari/Firefox behavior, and the impaired viewer network path remain unverified.
